A2.text: Published numbers use different scales and definitions from your 200 m method, so they are context only. The plan-comparable values must be computed from the DEMs.

H4.text: How to get the plan-comparable number

C5.text: Interior walls about 30 degrees (SELENE-based description). Not a 200 m mean.

E5.text: Wikipedia summary of Haruyama et al. 2008

H5.text: LOLA 5 m DEM (87-90S) or 20 m slope map; clip about 20 km, resample to 200 m (dataset #13).

H6.text: LOLA roughness map or std dev in a 1 km window (dataset #13).

C7.text: Floor average about 90 K, 88 K at the floor. Not a day/night range for the rim.

H7.text: Diviner GDR / Polar Resource Product (dataset #14). Fix one range definition first.

C8.text: Artemis III candidate region has a relatively flat area at about 86S 0E above a roughly 5,000 m relief; NASA lander requirement is under 5 degrees (conference slides). No numeric slope.

E8.text: LROC feature article; Artemis base camp slides

H8.text: LOLA 10 m or 20 m DEM (not the 5 m, which stops at 87S); dataset #13.

H11.text: MOLA-HRSC 200 m DEM, 20 km clip (dataset #18). Inspect for blend artifacts.

H12.text: Mars Climate Database, dataset #21. Record the dust scenario.

H13.text: Mars Climate Database dust column optical depth.

C17.text: LADEE measured the dust cloud around the Moon, not surface dust at a site, so no per-site value exists.
